notes: MCP TOOLS. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs that registers every tool of this crate. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (JSON.stringify(x, null, 2) corresponds to serde_json::to_string_pretty; serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). State the TypeScript keeps in module variables goes in a struct fetched with `ctx.state::<T>()`. The traffic store is `ctx.traffic` (rever_core::traffic); helpers already ported live in rever-formats (protobuf_decode), rever-analysis (token_decode, endpoints) and rever-core: use them as path dependencies instead of re-porting. crypto.ts uses Node's crypto module: use well-known Rust crates for the same algorithms (sha1, sha2, md-5, hmac, aes, base64, hex) and check outputs against the TypeScript with bun on a few vectors. Page access is only through `ctx.browser` (the `Browser` trait): where the TypeScript uses Chrome DevTools Protocol calls or Electron APIs, use the matching `Browser` method; when none matches, do NOT edit rever-tools-api: return `utils::err(tool::unsupported("<what>"))` from that code path, keep the argument validation and pure logic, and list the missing capability under behaviorDifferences in your report. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; you may add tokio and, for outbound HTTP, reqwest with rustls-tls; tests use #[tokio::test] and a fake `Browser` written in the test module. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
